en: The Apadāna of the Elder Khajjakadāyaka Supāricariyavagga, Chapter 3 [Verse 1] "I was a householder in the city of Benares, Possessing wealth and great riches. I gave various kinds of food To the monks who were free from desire. [Verse 2] "Having given that gift with a joyful heart, I passed away from that human existence. By the result of that wholesome deed, I was reborn in the world of the gods. [Verse 3] "In the realm of the Thirty-Three, I enjoyed divine pleasures. For eighty-four thousand years, I dwelt there in celestial bliss. [Verse 4] "When my lifespan there had come to an end, I passed away from that divine existence. By the result of that wholesome deed, I was reborn in the human world. [Verse 5] "In the city of Sāvatthī, I was born into a wealthy family. I possessed abundant wealth and grain, And was endowed with all forms of prosperity.

[Verse 6] "I gave various kinds of food To the monks who were free from desire. Because of that wholesome deed, I attained the fruit of Stream-entry. [Verse 7] "I have seen the Buddha, the One with Vision, The Teacher, the One of Great Wisdom. Having heard his Dhamma, I have crossed over the ocean of suffering. “To the Blessed One Tissa,
I formerly gave fruit;
I also offered him a coconut.”
Having given that well-prepared snack to the Buddha,
to Tissa, the Great Seer, I—
Desiring pleasures,
I was born wherever I wished;
ninety-two eons ago from now, I attained my desire.
The gift that I gave back then—
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of giving the gift.
In this thirteenth aeon,
there was a king equal to Indra,
endowed with the seven treasures.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Khajjakadāyaka recited these verses.
This is the third legend of the elder Khajjakadāyaka.
